A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPO research and are readable throughout, including equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained content can be reliably matched despite appendix restructuring.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.2 report original math and coding evaluations, component ablations, preference-list analyses and detailed MATH results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain original evaluations and add reasoning benchmarks, model backbones, comparison methods, sensitivity experiments and repeated-run statistical results.

M1.justification: Equation (10) changes the stated reward calculation: the semantic-similarity weight now multiplies the entire difference between step log-ratios, whereas v1 weights only the first term. This is a limited correction within Adaptive Step Reward; the other components and Algorithm 1 remain. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: V2 adds BBH multi-step reasoning and MMLU multiple-choice evaluations to the retained four math and two coding datasets (Section 4.1, Table 2). This substantially broadens out-of-distribution task coverage. The mathematical preference-training corpus remains unchanged.

E2.justification: SFT becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 1-2. Appendix C.2/Table 5 adds custom DPO* and DPO+ baselines constructed from top-versus-other and adjacent ranked preferences, respectively. Table 6 additionally compares Pointwise SoftMax, Pairwise Logistic and Listwise MLE against LambdaLoss. These are substantive additions to the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 backbones, BBH step-by-step and MMLU multiple-choice prompting, preference-pair construction controls, and a beta sweep over 0.5, 0.1 and 0.01. These expand the evaluation design; the original pass@1 metric and stated one-epoch training recipe are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds analyses of preference-data use, alternative ranking losses, statistical validation of Adaptive Step Reward, two reward-margin case studies and beta sensitivity. Conversely, v1's MATH difficulty and problem-type breakdowns in Appendix A.2 are removed. The original component ablations and preference-list analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4/Table 7 newly reports 20 independent experiments for each TPO/without-Adaptive-Step-Reward condition, performance means with standard errors, independent t-tests, exact p-values and significance markers. V1 reports variability in reward distributions but no corresponding repeated-run uncertainty or significance analysis of model performance.

E6.justification: Original numerical results in Tables 1-3 and Figure 3 are retained, but substantial new results cover SFT, additional backbones, BBH/MMLU, DPO variants, ranking losses, repeated-run estimates and beta settings. For example, new BBH results give Qwen2-7B TPO 69.62 versus DPO 65.58. These are added comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains. The earlier MATH subgroup results are removed.

T1.justification: Equation (10)'s revised weighting makes identical shared steps contribute zero, resolving the inconsistency between v1's printed formula and its stated cancellation property. V2 also explicitly explains that cancellation. The other core mathematical definitions and derivations remain, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract expands its claim of consistent superiority over DPO from three publicly available LLMs to five, retaining four math datasets. The stated contributions and conclusion are otherwise unchanged, so this is a limited expansion of claimed empirical scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets BBH improvements as transferred long-chain reasoning and stable MMLU performance as preserved knowledge. Appendix C adds explanations involving chosen-response likelihood decline, absolute ranking positions, semantic similarity versus token overlap, and the beta/forgetting trade-off. These substantially extend interpretation while retaining the original forgetting and reward-imbalance limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies exact BBH and MMLU prompts, while Appendix C specifies the new DPO pair constructions and TPO beta settings. Existing data-generation prompts, hardware, optimizer, learning rate and code-access information remain. This is a limited expansion of reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: New Appendix D and Table 9 explicitly position TPO against S-DPO, Rose-DPO and ODPO through their objectives and treatment of negative preferences, ranking positions and weighting. Additional ranking-loss, LambdaLoss and preference-optimization literature supports the expanded discussion. These related methods are not reported as direct empirical baselines.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence remain. V2 removes two introductory method-summary paragraphs, moves Algorithm 1 to Appendix A, reorganizes the appendix into algorithms, prompts, experiments and related literature, updates affiliations and conference headers, and adds acknowledgments. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Tables 1-2 gain SFT rows, and Table 2 gains grouped reasoning columns. V2 adds six appendix tables, a four-panel reward-margin Figure 4 and two case-study boxes, while removing v1's two MATH breakdown tables and relocating Algorithm 1. Figures 1-3 remain unchanged. This substantially changes the presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: The stronger preference-data controls, alternative-loss and beta comparisons, and 20-run significance tests substantially strengthen validation of TPO's central components, especially the previously unquantified small Adaptive Step Reward gains. Additional backbones and reasoning tasks improve assessment of generality, and Equation (10) is corrected. These benefits outweigh the loss of MATH subgroup detail and a flawed new Case 1, whose supposedly correct responses incorrectly calculate (5+3i)(5-3i) as 16.
